$comment: Evaluation sets of scripts/eval.py (Linear DEV-147). dev: rules may be tuned against these projects. held-out: never tuned against; labels, configuration and revision are frozen in FROZEN.json. A held-out project that drives a fix moves to dev (record it in `history`) and a new held-out project is added from `reserve`. Every project is Drizzle + PostgreSQL (the supported ORM); the first proposed held-out candidates (cal.com, dub, documenso, formbricks) use Prisma and were not eligible. Checkouts live under .corpora/ (git-ignored) and are never executed or modified.

projects.name: midday
projects.notes: The project the rules were developed against (Phases 2-16). Findings: Phase 2 review of a sample (from corpora/labels/midday.json). Known positives: source-only audit added 2026-11-06 (DEV-148), so dev recall includes midday.

projects.name: kan
projects.notes: Kanban app: tRPC routers over repository functions, email, webhooks, Stripe, S3. Moved to dev on 2026-11-12: the user requested analyzer fixes driven by these evaluation misses and false positives.

projects.name: dittofeed
projects.notes: Customer messaging: Postgres through db(), Temporal workflows, ClickHouse, Kafka, message providers. Moved to dev on 2026-11-12: the user requested analyzer fixes driven by these evaluation misses and false positives.

projects.name: zero
projects.notes: Email client on Cloudflare Workers: Drizzle, a database Durable Object, Gmail/Outlook APIs, queues, R2/KV. Moved from held-out to dev on 2026-11-06: its false positives (the generic `fetch` rule) are to be fixed, which is tuning against it.

projects.name: vercel-chatbot
projects.notes: Next.js AI chat template: Drizzle + postgres-js queries in lib/db/queries.ts, Vercel Blob uploads, Redis resumable streams and rate limiting. Promoted from reserve on 2026-11-06. Moved to dev on 2026-11-12: the user requested analyzer fixes driven by these evaluation misses and false positives.

projects.name: nextjs-billing
projects.notes: Lemon Squeezy billing template: Next.js server actions, Drizzle over Neon HTTP (no transactions), Lemon Squeezy SDK subscription calls and a webhook route that stores then processes events. Added as held-out on 2026-11-12 (HEAD of main): configuration written from source by an agent that did not run the analyzer, known positives from a separate source-only audit, findings classified by a third agent that saw neither.

projects.name: react-starter-kit
projects.notes: Bun monorepo starter: Hono + tRPC API, Better Auth with the Stripe plugin, Resend email, Drizzle over postgres-js (PostgreSQL). Added as held-out on 2026-11-12 (HEAD of main) by the DEV-161 sampling rule: configuration written from source by an agent that did not run the analyzer, known positives from a separate source-only audit, findings classified by a third agent that saw neither.

projects.name: petdex
projects.notes: Next.js gallery of animated pets: Drizzle over Neon HTTP (PostgreSQL), S3/R2 uploads, Resend email, Svix webhooks, Upstash Redis rate limiting, OpenAI. Added as held-out on 2026-11-12 (HEAD of main) by the DEV-161 sampling rule: configuration written from source by an agent that did not run the analyzer, known positives from a separate source-only audit, findings classified by a third agent that saw neither.

projects.name: next-saas-stripe-starter
projects.notes: Next.js SaaS starter: Better Auth with the Stripe plugin, Stripe SDK calls, Drizzle over Neon serverless (PostgreSQL). Added as held-out on 2026-11-12 (HEAD of main) by the DEV-161 sampling rule: configuration written from source by an agent that did not run the analyzer, known positives from a separate source-only audit, findings classified by a third agent that saw neither.

history.change: Sets created. Held-out configurations were written from the projects' source by agents that did not run the analyzer, before any held-out finding was looked at. Before that, one run with the default configuration only checked that the analyzer reaches each project's database code; its finding counts were seen, not the findings.

zero moved from held-out to dev: all 10 of its false positives in the first scoring come from the generic `fetch` configuration rule, and fixing that is tuning against it. Its frozen entry (revision 36132735, config 68ff38d2..., labels 2076f2b4...) was removed from FROZEN.json. vercel-chatbot promoted from reserve to held-out at a8989b52 (HEAD of main on 2026-11-06): configuration written from source before the analyzer was run on it, known positives from a source-only audit, findings classified by a separate agent. The reserve is now empty.
midday gets audited known positives (30, source-only audit that did not see Midwrite output) in corpora/eval/labels/midday.json, so dev recall is no longer zero-only (DEV-148).

kan, dittofeed and vercel-chatbot moved from held-out to dev before analyzer tuning requested by the user. Their source-grounded label-correction baseline is reports/eval/2026-11-12-label-corrections.json. No unused reserve project exists, so there is currently no independent held-out set; subsequent results on these projects are development comparisons, not held-out generalization scores.

react-starter-kit, petdex and next-saas-stripe-starter added as held-out (DEV-161), chosen by a fixed sampling rule: the first three eligible projects in `gh search repos --topic drizzle-orm --language typescript --sort stars` (OSI license, application with commits in the last 12 months, Drizzle on PostgreSQL in server code, an external-effect SDK in server code, never used in Midwrite development). Each pinned at the HEAD of its default branch. Configuration, source-only audit and finding labels came from three separate AI agents per project; all were frozen before scoring. See docs/development/evaluation-harness.md#held-out-set-restored-2026-11-12.
